aiDescription.summary: The bill permanently establishes an Emergency Safety and Security Grant Program in the U.S. Housing Act of 1937, authorizes $225 million annually, and directs HUD to award grants to public housing agencies for purchase, installation, repair, or replacement of security and safety items. Eligible items include cameras, fencing, lighting, alarms, locks, CO/smoke detectors, and heating fixes; per‑agency cap $250,000 (exceptions for extra‑large or >5,000 units).

description.text: To amend the United States Housing Act of 1937 to permanently authorize the emergency safety and security grant program, and for other purposes.

impact.summary: The bill requires HUD to make permanent an Emergency Safety and Security Grant program, authorizes $225 million yearly plus a Capital Fund set‑aside, and awards grants to public housing agencies (PHAs). Grants fund security and safety items—cameras, lighting, locks, CO/smoke detectors, heating fixes—with a $250,000 cap per PHA unless extra‑large or >5,000 units, affecting HUD, PHAs, residents, and contractors.

latestAction.text: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
